text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1719909999 Runtime OOM & container restarts on inference-pool-6 (paged-attn allocator high fragmentation). 6 nodes flapping, 3 containers restarted in last 7m. error: "CUDA out of memory / allocator assert". svc=redwood-infer-prod model=ggml-13b-q4. Alert: https://alerts.internal/redwood/alert/1719909999 :rotating_light:

sam: Ack, I'm taking lead. Marking P1. Starting triage — grabbing logs and heap stats. @priya can you scope customer impact (CS)? @miguel can you pull core + nvml metrics from the affected hosts?

priya: On it. Reached out to support-slack, CS shows 2 customers with elevated 503 rates on embedding route (~4-6% errors for last 10m). Add to incident summary.

miguel: running remote commands now. tl;dr from node-6-3: multiple "allocator: paged_attn::alloc failed" and repeated small allocations not reclaimed. CUDA OOM trace:
```
E/cuda: failed to allocate 512MB (out of memory)
allocator: paged_attn: free_list fragmentation -> can't satisfy 64k chunk in hot-shard(12)
stack: serve::kv::get_kv -> paged_attn::alloc -> cuda::alloc -> RuntimeError
```
I also see lots of small leaked pages in the KV slab bitmap (hot shards). Dumping slab stats to s3: s3://redwood-dumps/1719909999/slab-node-6-3.txt

sam: Good. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain worst nodes, 2) disable live-batching / reduce max_batch_size on affected pool, 3) route traffic away from prod pool to warm fallback + smaller model variant (ggml-13b-q4-lite), 4) bump eviction aggressiveness (kv.evict_threshold -> 0.6), 5) collect core dumps and kv metrics for postmortem.

rebecca: I'm pushing route rule to failover to dedicated warm pool for low-latency tier. ETA 2m. Will also open a temporary throttle for embeddings to keep token QPS down.

sam: Commands I'm running now:
```bash
# drain node
kubectl -n inference drain node-6-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# reduce batching
kubectl -n infra patch cm inference-pool-6 --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"8","enable_live_batching":"false"}}'
# toggle eviction
kubectl -n infra exec configmapctl -- sh -c "update-config kv.evict_threshold=0.6 && rollout restart ds/allocator"
```

miguel: Core and nvml traces uploaded: s3://redwood-dumps/1719909999/{node-6-3,n-6-4}.tgz. I also pushed a short diagnostic that runs the compact path on live slab (non-blocking):
```bash
# trigger compaction (experimental):
/redwood/bin/kvctl compact --shard 12 --background
```
Note: compaction reduces fragmentation but is I/O heavy; we'll monitor GPU/PCIe.

priya: Customer impact update: CS flagged corp-VEGA and startup-PL as seeing degraded embedding latency + increased 503s. Recommending a customer notice: "We experienced elevated errors on our Hosted inference pool due to memory fragmentation; traffic was routed to a stable fallback. Engineers are mitigating; we'll follow up with root cause." Want approval to send.

sam: Approve. Keep it short: mention mitigation and ETA for full restore (T+2h estimate).

eng-runtime-bot: New ticket created ENG-RUNTIME-1429: investigate paged-attn slab fragmentation + autoreclaim. Linked to incident 1719909999. Assigned to @miguel and @rebecca.

rebecca: Rolling restart of allocator ds started on drained nodes (node-6-3 done, node-6-4 in progress). Observed immediate drop in allocation failures on node-6-3. Still seeing slow rise on node-6-4.

sam: If restarts stabilize, plan is to ramp traffic back slowly over 15m. If allocation failures recur, fallback to dedicated capacity. Also we should flip kv.metrics retention to high-res for 1h to collect more samples.

miguel: One oddity: the leak appears correlated with a sequence-length skew — many requests with sle=4096 causing repeated small page churn in shard 12. Could be a kernel path not compacting split pages. Adding hypothesis to ticket.

priya: Noted. CS updated customers and queued the external notice.

angela: I'm taking night handoff at T+45m. Summary for handoff: cause suspected paged-attn allocator fragmentation leading to CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Mitigations applied: drained worst nodes, reduced batching, routed to fallback model, started slab compaction and allocator restarts, raised eviction aggressiveness. Current status: 2 nodes healthy, 2 nodes stable but watched, 2 nodes removed from pool. Customer impact: two customers with 4-6% 503s; overall platform error rate peaked at 3.8%. Followups: collect full kv slab dumps, add unit tests for compaction path, evaluate autoreclaim.

sam: Thanks @angela. Handoff checklist: attach links to dumps, ticket ENG-RUNTIME-1429, set pager if failures >1/min.

angela: Acknowledged. I'll keep watch and escalate if new restarts occur. Leaving note for postmortem: timeline + config change that reduced batch size.

sam: Postmortem owners: @miguel (root cause) and @rebecca (mitigation/ops changes). I'll draft initial incident timeline.

incident-bot: Incident 1719909999 status -> mitigated (partial) at 1719911200. Severity: Sev2. Followup: ENG-RUNTIME-1429 created.

angela: Handoff complete. Logging final state and leaving oncall. :thumbsup:
